## Data Source
This dataset provides us with data from two main sources:CDC Wonder and KFF (Kaiser Family Foundation). The CDC wonder datasets provide mortality and population data , while the KFF datasets provide state-level Medicare and Medicaid data. The information from this lists all states , along with their income and medicare and medicaid use defend the notion of increasing healthcare spending in certain states. Five useful data elements would be State,Population,Mortality/Deaths,Medicare/Medicaid Spending and income. Data elements State/Character, Population/Numeric, Deaths/numeric, Medicare spending/numeric, income/numeric.Data elements State/Character, Population/Numeric, Deaths/numeric, Medicare spending/numeric, income/numeric

```{r part2}

# PART 2: MORTALITY AND POPULATION — AGES 65+

# 1. LOAD PACKAGES -----------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(readr)


# 2. LOAD BOTH FILES BEFORE USING THEM ----------------------

mortality <- read_csv(
  "cdc_wonder_mortality.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

population <- read_csv(
  "cdc_wonder_population.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Remove extra spaces around column names
names(mortality) <- trimws(names(mortality))
names(population) <- trimws(names(population))

print(names(mortality))
print(names(population))


# 3. CHECK REQUIRED COLUMNS --------------------------------

mortality_columns <- c(
  "Residence State",
  "Residence State Code",
  "Ten-Year Age Groups",
  "Ten-Year Age Groups Code",
  "UCD - ICD Sub-Chapter",
  "UCD - ICD Sub-Chapter Code",
  "Deaths"
)

population_columns <- c(
  "State",
  "Ten-Year Age Groups",
  "Population"
)

if (!all(mortality_columns %in% names(mortality))) {
  stop(
    "Missing mortality columns: ",
    paste(
      setdiff(mortality_columns, names(mortality)),
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

if (!all(population_columns %in% names(population))) {
  stop(
    "Missing population columns: ",
    paste(
      setdiff(population_columns, names(population)),
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    ". Check names(population)."
  )
}


# 4. DEFINE A FUNCTION FOR SUMMING COUNTS -------------------

# Keep NA if every count is missing
sum_available <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}


# 5. CLEAN MORTALITY AND IDENTIFY AGES 65+ -------------------

mortality_clean <- mortality %>%
  rename(
    state = `Residence State`,
    age_group = `Ten-Year Age Groups`,
    icd_subchapter = `UCD - ICD Sub-Chapter`,
    icd_code = `UCD - ICD Sub-Chapter Code`,
    deaths = Deaths
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state = toupper(trimws(state)),
    age_group = trimws(age_group),
    icd_code = trimws(as.character(icd_code)),
    deaths = parse_number(as.character(deaths)),
    age_65_plus = grepl("^(65|75|85)", age_group)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    state %in% c(toupper(state.name), "DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA")
  )

# Check the age labels selected
print(
  mortality_clean %>%
    filter(age_65_plus) %>%
    distinct(age_group)
)

if (!any(mortality_clean$age_65_plus)) {
  stop("No mortality ages 65+ matched. Check the age labels.")
}


# 6. FIND THE TOP TWO ICD SUB-CHAPTERS ----------------------

top_2_icd <- mortality_clean %>%
  filter(
    age_65_plus,
    !is.na(icd_subchapter),
    trimws(icd_subchapter) != "",
    !is.na(icd_code),
    icd_code != ""
  ) %>%
  group_by(icd_code, icd_subchapter) %>%
  summarise(
    total_deaths = sum_available(deaths),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_deaths)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_deaths), icd_code) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2)

if (nrow(top_2_icd) != 2) {
  stop("Fewer than two ICD sub-chapters have usable death counts.")
}

# Display the selected ICD codes and names
print(top_2_icd)


# 7. CREATE THE INTERMEDIATE KEEP/REMOVE COLUMN -------------

mortality_clean <- mortality_clean %>%
  mutate(
    keep_row = age_65_plus &
      icd_code %in% top_2_icd$icd_code
  )

mortality_top_2 <- mortality_clean %>%
  filter(keep_row)


# 8. SUMMARIZE MORTALITY TO ONE ROW PER STATE ---------------

mortality_by_state <- mortality_top_2 %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(
    total_deaths_65_plus = sum_available(deaths),
    missing_death_counts = sum(is.na(deaths)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    selected_icd_codes = paste(
      top_2_icd$icd_code,
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    selected_icd_subchapters = paste(
      top_2_icd$icd_subchapter,
      collapse = "; "
    )
  )

print(mortality_by_state)


# 9. CLEAN POPULATION AND IDENTIFY AGES 65+ ------------------

population_clean <- population %>%
  rename(
    state = State,
    age_group = `Ten-Year Age Groups`,
    population_count = Population
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Change "01-Alabama" to "ALABAMA"
    state = toupper(
      trimws(sub("^[0-9]+\\s*-\\s*", "", state))
    ),
    age_group = trimws(age_group),
    population_count = parse_number(as.character(population_count)),
    age_65_plus = age_group %in% c(
      "65-74 years",
      "75-84 years",
      "85+ years"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    state %in% c(toupper(state.name), "DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA")
  )

print(
  population_clean %>%
    filter(age_65_plus) %>%
    distinct(age_group)
)

if (!any(population_clean$age_65_plus)) {
  stop("No population ages 65+ matched. Check the age labels.")
}

# Review repeated state/age rows before summing
population_duplicates <- population_clean %>%
  filter(age_65_plus) %>%
  count(state, age_group) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

if (nrow(population_duplicates) > 0) {
  print(population_duplicates)
  stop("Repeated state/age rows need review before summing population.")
}


# 10. SUMMARIZE POPULATION TO ONE ROW PER STATE -------------

population_by_state <- population_clean %>%
  filter(age_65_plus) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(
    population_65_plus = sum_available(population_count),
    missing_population_counts = sum(is.na(population_count)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(population_by_state)


# 11. COMBINE MORTALITY AND POPULATION ----------------------

part2_data <- full_join(
  mortality_by_state,
  population_by_state,
  by = "state"
) %>%
  arrange(state)

print(part2_data)

# Show missing or incomplete results
checks_needed <- part2_data %>%
  filter(
    is.na(total_deaths_65_plus) |
      is.na(population_65_plus) |
      missing_death_counts > 0 |
      missing_population_counts > 0
  )

print(checks_needed)

# Confirm one row per state
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(part2_data$state))


# 12. EXPORT RESULTS ---------------------------------------

write_csv(
  part2_data,
  "part2_mortality_population_65_plus.csv"
)

write_csv(
  top_2_icd,
  "part2_selected_icd_subchapters.csv"
)

# Show the folder containing the exported files
getwd()

```
